title: Filtered colimits and higher direct image
statement:
If $u:U\to V$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $(F_i)$ is a filtered system of torsion
etale sheaves [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], then for every $q\geq0$ the
canonical map

$$
 \varinjlim_iR^qu_*F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}R^qu_*(\varinjlim_iF_i)
$$

involving the higher direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] is an
isomorphism. The same assertion holds after arbitrary base change.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09Z1 (lemma-relative-colimit), proof; Cohomology on Sites Lemma Tag 03Q5 for the cohomology-colimit input

proof.text: For an etale object $W\to V$, the higher-direct-image description [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-higher-direct-image] identifies $(R^qu_*F_i)(W)$ and $(R^qu_*\varinjlim_iF_i)(W)$ after sheafification with $H^q(W\times_VU,F_i|)$ and $H^q(W\times_VU,(\varinjlim_iF_i)|)$, respectively. The comparison is natural in $W$ and in the coefficient sheaves, by the definition of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

source.place: Lemma Tag 09Z1, proof: recall the higher-direct-image sheafification description

proof.text: Every etale $W\to V$ has a covering by affine etale objects; on such a quasi-compact quasi-separated $W$, the fibre product $W\times_VU$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The filtered-colimit cohomology theorem [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit] therefore gives a canonical isomorphism $\varinjlim_i H^q(W\times_VU,F_i|)\cong H^q(W\times_VU,\varinjlim_iF_i|)$. The same statement holds on finite fibre products of the affine basis objects, so these isomorphisms form an isomorphism of the associated presheaves after restricting to that basis. In the source-library realization, maps from the degree-zero free sheaf on the terminal object shifted by $q\geq0$ identify naturally with underlying module derived cohomology by [lem-weil-pbc-free-sheaf-derived-sections]. Apply the module clause of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit], then forget module structure (which preserves colimits) and transport along this natural isomorphism. For the additional Lean case $q<0$, maps between degree-zero sheaves with this shift vanish by t-structure orthogonality; the resulting zero functor preserves all colimits.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09Z1, proof: quasi-compact etale objects and the equality of cohomology colimits; underlying cohomology input is Tag 03Q5

proof.text: The inverse image of sheaves commutes with filtered colimits because [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-preserves-colimits] identifies it as a left adjoint. Colimits of abelian sheaves are sheafifications of presheaf colimits, and sheafification preserves colimits; filtered colimits are exact by [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaves-filtered-colimits-exact]. Thus sheafifying the basiswise cohomology isomorphisms yields the canonical isomorphism $\varinjlim_iR^qu_*F_i\xrightarrow{\sim}R^qu_*(\varinjlim_iF_i)$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09Z1, proof: colimits of sheaves are sheafified presheaf colimits and the final sheafification argument

proof.text: After an arbitrary base change $V'\to V$, the base-changed morphism $U\times_VV'\to V'$ remains quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Repeating the preceding three steps for this morphism proves the asserted base-change form, with the same canonical maps and naturality.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09Z1, proof applied after base change

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes $h:W\to V$ and a
filtered system of torsion sheaves $(F_i)$, the canonical map

$$
\varinjlim_i R^qh_*F_i\longrightarrow R^qh_*(\varinjlim_iF_i)
$$

is an isomorphism for every $q$.
blueprint_sketch.proof:
For $q=0$, sections on a quasi-compact etale object are the equalizer of a
finite covering diagram after a finite quasi-compact refinement; filtered
colimits commute with this finite limit. For $q>0$, represent a class by a
degree-$q$ cocycle on a split etale hypercover with finite $(q+1)$-skeleton.
Each of its finitely many sections is represented in some $F_i$, and the
finite list of face-map equalities holds at one later index because the system
is filtered. This proves surjectivity of
$\varinjlim_iH^q(W,F_i)\to H^q(W,\varinjlim_iF_i)$.

If a class from $F_i$ dies after the colimit, choose a finite hypercover
refinement and a degree-$(q-1)$ null-homotopy on the limit. Its finitely many
sections, refinement maps, and equations descend to one index $j\geq i$;
there the class is already a coboundary. Thus the map is injective. The
same argument applies after every quasi-compact etale base change
$U\to V$, so the cohomology-sheaf description of $R^qh_*$ identifies the
displayed sheaves. This is the derived filtered-colimit argument, with no
unbounded injective replacement required.
